Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Mining | National Gold Fields says Tarkwa mine has contributed US$3.3bn to Ghana 17 November 2026 5:39pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Gold Fields Ghana Limited says it has paid US$3.3 billion to the Government of Ghana in royalties, corporate taxes and dividends from its operations at the Tarkwa mine.
In a media statement issued on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the company also disclosed that it had invested more than US$5 billion in developing and sustaining the mine.
The statement comes as the government reviews the company's application to renew the Tarkwa mining leases. Gold Fields said it submitted the application in November 2025, following a request from the government to do so early.
Gold Fields said it was among the mining companies invited to invest in Ghana in the early 1990s as part of efforts to revive the country's gold sector.
At the time, Tarkwa was a loss-making underground mine operated by the State Gold Mining Corporation, producing approximately 12,000 ounces of gold annually and approaching closure, according to the company.
In 1992, the government selected Gold Fields as its preferred investor, leading to the signing of a project development agreement under which the company paid US$3 million.
Gold Fields said it subsequently invested US$50 million in exploration from 1993, leading to the identification of the open-pit resource.
The government granted five mining leases in 1997, allowing the company to develop the open-pit mine currently in operation. Gold Fields said it separately paid US$8 million for assets transferred from the former underground operation, following a government valuation.
The company said its total investment in Tarkwa has since exceeded US$5 billion, covering the development of open pits, the processing plant and supporting infrastructure.
Managing Director of Gold Fields Ghana, Elliot Twum, said the company had invested in exploration, defined the resource and developed a large-scale operation that had generated value for Ghana over several decades.
He said the company respected the government's lease renewal process and the views of host communities.
“Subject to the outcome of that process, we are ready to make the investment Tarkwa needs for its next phase,” he stated.
Gold Fields said it had spent more than US$4.6 billion with local suppliers over the past five years, supporting businesses including Engineers & Planners, Zen Petroleum, Genser Energy and Western Transport Services.
The mine supports a workforce of more than 5,000 people, comprising employees and contractors, the company said.
It added that its operations prioritise safety and responsible environmental management, while the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation had invested more than US$114 million in community projects.
The company said it remained committed to engaging host communities and investing in priorities identified through consultations with them.
It acknowledged concerns raised in recent weeks and said it would continue working with traditional authorities, municipal assemblies and community representatives to address local needs.
Gold Fields said mining benefits reached communities through both direct investments by companies and the government's allocation of public revenue, including taxes and royalties.
It argued that lasting improvements depended on cooperation among the government, mining companies and host communities.
The company also acknowledged support from some traditional leaders and civil society representatives, including those involved in the “Gold Fields must stay” campaign.
Gold Fields said the Tarkwa mine required substantial additional investment in waste stripping, tailings capacity, its mining fleet and processing plant to extend its operating life.
It said the investment would also be important to sustaining employment, local procurement and public revenue associated with the mine.
The company cited its technical expertise, experience operating Tarkwa, access to financing and established environmental management standards as factors positioning it to undertake the next phase of work.
It reiterated that it was prepared to make the investment, subject to the outcome of the lease renewal process.
The government is expected to complete its review of Gold Fields' application to renew the Tarkwa mining leases.
Gold Fields is a global gold producer with eight operating mines in Australia, South Africa, Ghana, Chile and Peru, as well as a project in Canada. Its shares are listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, while its American depositary shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
